extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and editing ProofWiki content (book pages, proofs, definitions, discussion posts) consistent with site house style and technical/procedural conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use site notation and record idiosyncratic notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ProofWiki (Pr∞fWiki) notation, and add idiosyncratic notation in an 'also denoted as' / 'also presented as' / 'also defined as' subsection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the site's notation conventions; when a source uses idiosyncratic notation, record it explicitly in a dedicated subsection so readers understand deviations from site norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include historical context via a 'historical note' section
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, provide historical context for books or results using a 'historical note' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add historical remarks in a dedicated subsection to document provenance or notable historical commentary on the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the book's ToC style for book pages
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no forced canonical ToC format; follow the style used in the book when creating a book contents page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce the book's table-of-contents style where practical; for lengthy or tedious reproduction you may include only main chapter headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notability criterion for separate book pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a separate page for a different edition/printing only when the change is notable; avoid creating nearly duplicate pages for every minor printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors' judgment is trusted; minor changes (typos fixed, small prefaces) typically do not justify a new page, whereas substantive new content may.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not paste full book contents without access to the book
rubrics_metrics.description: Only paste book contents if you have the book to hand and can verify fair use; do not paste contents from books you cannot see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProofWiki avoids reproducing material unless the contributor has legitimate access and the reproduction is appropriate under copyright/fair-use considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include page numbers on book pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Page numbers are generally omitted because different printings/editions may have different pagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attaching page numbers to content to prevent maintenance burden from differing printings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to first page in a linear ordering when useful
rubrics_metrics.description: For strictly linear orderings (paths through works), it is generally good practice to include a link to the first page in that ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your book/page sequence corresponds to an ordered path, include a link to the first page so readers can follow the sequence easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline and split very long proofs into subpages
rubrics_metrics.description: For long proofs (e.g., proofs spanning many articles/pages), provide an outline on the main proof page and break the proof into conceptual sections, giving each subproof its own page linked from the main page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with an outline. Break the argument into logical pieces, make separate pages for each subproof, and link; use existing big proofs (e.g., Poincaré Conjecture page) as a model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post to a page's discussion via the 'Discussion' tab
rubrics_metrics.description: To add material to a discussion page, click the 'Discussion' link at the top of the page; a blue link means the page exists, red means you will create it by posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the discussion tab is blue, add to the existing talk page; if red, your contribution will create the talk page. This is the standard procedure for discussion posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbounded quantifier convention: use colons between quantifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: For unbounded quantification use the form ∀x: ∀y: ∃a: (…) — colons are used (loosely) to mean 'such that'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the colon convention for clarity; this is stated as the site's quantifier convention and preferred by maintainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded quantifiers: use commas to list multiple variables over same set
rubrics_metrics.description: When the same quantifier ranges over the same set (e.g., ∀x ∈ R and ∀y ∈ R), shorten to the comma form ∀x, y ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commas separate entities in a list; use the comma-shortening when both variables share the same domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use comma to mean 'such that' after set membership; use colon
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid constructs like ∀x ∈ S, P x which use a comma to mean 'such that'; instead write ∀x ∈ S: P x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commas must not serve as 'such that' separators — change such uses to the colon convention to comply with house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer dollar-sign math delimiters ($…$) over <math> tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Use $…$ delimiters for inline math rather than <math>, because <math> is not fully supported by MathJax and dollars are more compact and quicker to type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dollar delimiters for MathJax compatibility and brevity; site maintainers explicitly recommend this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer formalized quantifiers over natural language unless confusing
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalized quantifiers are preferred in proofs/pages, unless that formalization makes the text highly confusing; in such cases natural language may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for formal notation for precision; fallback to prose only when it increases clarity for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use export tools responsibly; prefer site XML dump for large data needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Export Pages' special tool exists but running large exports can degrade site performance. For large-scale needs, use the provided XML dumps (e.g., https://proofwiki.org/xmldump/latest.xml.gz) and contact administrators for heavy operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not run heavy exports frequently; coordinate with site admins (User talk:Joe) to avoid overloading the server. A periodic official dump is preferred for ML/data work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using the MediaWiki API to mass-dump content without coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Siphoning the site via the API or frequent automated exports is discouraged because it can render the site unusable for others; contact the main administrator before attempting large-scale fetching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you require full dumps for legitimate purposes (offline wiki, ML research), ask administrators and use official dumps to prevent heavy load on the live site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting proofs: create a page, choose a good name, and leave proof for others
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofWiki does not provide personal assistance; to request a proof, create a page for the theorem with a good name and leave the proof for someone else to fill in (or ask on an external Q&A forum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a page with a clear title (example suggestion provided) and either draft an outline or wait for contributors to add the detailed proof; external Q&A sites are recommended for faster personal help.

rubrics_metrics.name: House style for layout: left-aligned content and QED on the left
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything on the site 'hangs to the left' as house style; the QED box ({{qed}}) is placed on the left beneath proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to align boxes to the right; follow the house style of left alignment and short sentences to avoid wide right-side layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to create a 'Definition' page
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a page as a 'Definition' when the content is the definition of something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the term/object has a definitional status, make it a Definition page. Also, when editing help pages, avoid interrupting existing Q/A pairs — use history comparison tools to see changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ambiguous uses of the word 'any'
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'any' is ambiguous — it can mean 'an arbitrary element' or 'there exists' — and should be replaced with a more precise structure under house style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you find 'any' in writing, replace it with explicit quantifiers or clearer wording to remove ambiguity. If unsure in a specific case, raise it on the relevant talk page with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact administrators via talk pages for admin tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact an administrator or request administrative help (e.g., site dumps), use the administrator's talk page (e.g., User talk:Joe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative coordination should be done via talk pages rather than heavy automated actions on the live site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use site examples of style as models (e.g., Vector Space Axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to existing pages that illustrate ProofWiki style (e.g., 'Vector Space Axioms') as models to emulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about formatting or phrasing, copy stylistic choices from well-formed existing pages on the site.
